english.title: Give / employ another to give paid driving instruction when not registered / licenced to do so
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[gave]_
(B)_[employed a person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to give]_

paid instruction in the driving of a motor car when

(C)_[you were not]_
(D)_[the employee was not]_

(E)_[named in the register of approved instructors established in pursuance of section 23 of the Road Traffic Act 1962]_
(F)_[the holder of a current licence granted under Part V of the Road Traffic Act 1988 authorising the giving of such instruction]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 123(1) and (4) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) Section 123(5) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that In proceedings against a person for an offence under section 123(4) it shall be a defence for him to prove that he did not know, and had no reasonable cause to believe, that his name or, as the case may be, that of the person employed by him, was not in the register at the material time.
(ii) Section 123(2) of the Road Traffic act 1988 provides that no paid instruction in the driving of a motor car shall be given unless there is fixed to and exhibited on that motor car in such manner as may be prescribed by regulations either:-
(a) a certificate in such form as may be so prescribed that the name of the instructor is in the register, OR
(b) a current licence granted under this Part of this Act authorising the instructor to give such instruction.
(iii) Section 123(4) of the Road Traffic act 1988 provides that where another person is employed to give the driving instruction BOTH the employer AND the employee commit an offence.
